briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 12, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Major Impacts
sections.content: According to news released today, large-scale wildfires in Indonesia, influenced by El Niño, have led to warnings that 2026 emissions are on track to match this century's record [31]. This aligns with reports that Australia and Canada are experiencing direct consequences of climate change, such as worsening wildfires, floods, and droughts, while operating mining, oil, and gas-based economic models [30]. Furthermore, serious concerns have been raised that climate change, mobility, and conflict could lead to a 'world of climate refugees' [28]. There's even a forecast that climate change could increase the alcohol content of champagne to 15%, suggesting unexpected impacts on our daily lives [29].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Skepticism in Climate Action
sections.content: Efforts to address climate change continue to face significant challenges. In the United States, resistance to the clean energy transition is considerable, with a total of 567 renewable energy projects encountering opposition, leading to approximately 40% being canceled [8]. Furthermore, 20 years after the release of 'An Inconvenient Truth,' questions about climate change are still being raised [21]. A fact-check also revealed that Reform UK, which has emerged as a major force in British politics, made 45 false or misleading claims regarding climate and energy [32]. The omission of key discussions on climate change at the Pacific Gray Whale Symposium held in Newport demonstrates how such skepticism and indifference are permeating even important public forums [22].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Change Response and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst these crises, domestic and international efforts to address climate change are steadily continuing. In response to the increasing burden on electricity and water due to expanded domestic semiconductor production, Samsung and SK are increasing their use of renewable energy and water recycling [9]. The food industry is also participating in the carbon-neutral transition by expanding solar power and high-efficiency facilities in their factories [13]. Asan City Carbon Neutral Support Center is striving to improve awareness by conducting carbon neutrality and ESG education for kindergarten directors [6]. KEPCO KPS and Chosun University are encouraging the participation of future generations through the launch ceremony of the youth-led 'ESG Youth-lab' [7]. Internationally, the Dominican Republic, in collaboration with the Netherlands and INTEC, is focusing on developing practical adaptation solutions, such as exploring climate change adaptation strategies [24].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Policy and New Technology Trends
sections.content: Policy discussions and technological developments for addressing climate change are also actively underway. Ahead of COP31, despite Australia leading negotiations, Türkiye asserted its 'final decision-making power,' highlighting the complexities of international climate negotiations [25]. Meanwhile, the emergence of EREVs (Extended Range Electric Vehicles), which have a fuel filler but use gasoline to generate electricity for motors rather than directly powering the wheels, has sparked debate over whether they are truly eco-friendly or merely a market 'painkiller' [15]. In this context, voices like a reader's submission emphasizing the need for accurate facts on climate change underscore the importance of information and the necessity to enhance public understanding [26].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, the various efforts being made to address it, and the challenges that still persist. We must not cease our efforts towards a sustainable future through accurate information, international cooperation, and technological innovation. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: Extended Range Electric Vehicles (EREVs) are emerging, featuring a fuel filler but with engines that do not directly drive the wheels; instead, they burn fuel to generate electricity to power the motors. These vehicles reduce battery size to cut weight and cost, offering a driving range of up to 960km.
summary.cause: EREVs were developed as a compromise to reduce vehicle weight and cost by decreasing battery size, while simultaneously ensuring a long driving range. This approach is particularly useful in the large SUV and pickup truck markets.
summary.outlook: EREVs have the potential for an extended lifespan, coinciding with eased US emission regulations and the EU's shift towards technological neutrality. They could serve as a stepping stone for the transition to electric vehicles, moving beyond a mere temporary measure.
